lines.text: What if a whole year of *snow* fell on New York... in five seconds?
Central Park gets about *thirty inches* of snow in an average year.
Seventy-six centimeters. Cars buried up to their doors.
Melt all of that snow... and you'd get only about *seven centimeters* of water.
Fresh snow is mostly *air*. Around ninety percent.
A year of rain would flood this street over a meter deep.
Follow for more. What should fall next?
